messages:
maya: Quick sync — we keep seeing orphaned sampled spans when late enrichment attaches billing keys. How do we want to handle reassembling sampled traces across the ingest pipeline?
aj: Can you paste a short example of the orphan pattern you saw?
maya: Sure. flow: edge -> service A (sample=1) -> service B (not-sampled) -> enrichment service adds billing_key later. Because B dropped spans, when we stitch by trace_id the sampled span arrives first and enrichment comes with billing later so cost attribution misses.
aj: So it's a timing/ordering issue, not missing IDs.
lee: Two quick approaches: 1) attach a small "sampled_marker" envelope at the edge that persists until enrichment joins; 2) make enrichment do a lookup against recent sampled trace set. Tradeoffs in storage + latency.
chris: Option 1 sounds cheaper on CPU but increases ingress size and retention window. Option 2 adds a query per enrich event, which could spike QPS.
olivia: Also consider route-level batching: if enrichment is delayed only slightly, a short-lived in-memory cache (LRU with TTL) in the enrichment consumer might be enough.
maya: TTL needs to be tuned: we observed delays up to 45s in some backfills and retries. LRU+45s = lot of memory on hot pods.
aj: Could be sharded by tenant. Hot tenants pay the memory cost; cold tenants have best-effort reassembly.
lee: We also discussed keeping a compact index in Kafka for sampled trace headers: a tiny topic keyed by trace_id with last-seen timestamp and sampled_marker. Enrichment could do an async read (lightweight) using the Kafka log via RocksDB local store (like a changelog). More operational complexity but bounded storage.
chris: That aligns with our stream-processing mindset. But we need idempotency: race where marker written after enrichment read.
maya: We can have enrichment write a tombstone if it can't find marker, then a reconciler job can sweep tombstones and reconcile with late markers — but that adds another background job and potential double-counting windows.
olivia: For cost attribution correctness we need deterministic rules. Suggestion: attribution rule = if any sampled_marker seen within window W of the span timestamp, attribute to sampled cohort; otherwise default.
aj: Define W = 2 minutes for now as a configurable knob per tenant. Longer window increases false positives.
lee: Implementation sketch in protos:
```
message SamplingMarker {
  string trace_id = 1;
  int64 ts_ms = 2;
  string tenant_id = 3;
}
```
and a compact store that holds only (trace_id -> ts_ms, bitflags) for W.
chris: Operational questions: retention sizing math, cross-az replication, and metrics to detect when enrichment misses markers (i.e., leakage signal).
maya: Metrics we need: marker_emitted, marker_lookup_hit, marker_lookup_miss, reconcilations_run, attribution_delta_percent. Also a tag metric by tenant.
olivia: For rollout: 1) emit markers at edge for a small % of traffic (canary) 2) run enrichment lookup in shadow read path and record hits/misses 3) switch attribution for canary tenants 4) expand.
aj: Can we avoid changing SDKs at edge? We can inject marker in proxy sidecar or edge lambda so most customers unaffected.
lee: SDK change optional. Proxy + edge-router is ideal — single place.
chris: Also add a debug flag to force emit for a trace_id for offline repro: `X-Debug-Sample: force-marker`.
maya: Action items: 
- (maya) write short RFC with the two designs (compact Kafka-changelog store vs enrichment LRU) and cost math. Due EOD Thursday.
- (aj) prototype shadow lookup in enrichment consumer (1 day).
- (lee) sizing calc for W=15s, 45s, 120s and tenant percentiles (1 day).
- (olivia) define metrics + dashboards (alerts for miss rate > 0.5% for top 10 tenants).
- (chris) propose reconciliation approach if we get significant late joins (investigate tombstone reconciler complexity).

maya: Anything else?
aj: Can we add simulated load to perf-test the RocksDB local lookup latency? I'll add to perf board.
lee: FYI edge-proxy team already has a hook to add small headers, I'll talk to them.
olivia: SGTM. I'll draft the dashboard panels and SLIs.
chris: If we need to avoid budget surprises, we can start with a very small canary tenant set and keep a tight W.
maya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link here once it's up. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for enrichment-consumer-v2 on prod-canary (id: d-8392)
maya: noted, thanks bot. We'll keep an eye on marker_lookup_miss metrics during the canary.
